rows: Key audit matter | How our audit addressed the key audit matter

The Company recorded revenue rebates and sales returns amounting to US$1,449 million in the consolidated statement of operations for the year ended December 31, 2025, 73% of which was related to sales chargebacks, rebates, returns and other deductions arising from the sale of products in the United States. The Company recognizes revenue when the transfer of control of goods or services to the customer is completed. To determine the appropriate transaction price at the time revenue is recognized, the Company estimates variable consideration related to sales chargebacks and rebates that will ultimately be due to the customer and others in the distribution channel under the terms of their contracts. Where appropriate, these estimates take into consideration, among other items, the Company's historical experience, current contractual and statutory requirements, and channel inventory levels. The Company recognizes revenue related to variable consideration to the extent it is probable that a significant revenue reversal will not occur and estimates variable consideration from sales chargebacks and rebates using the expected value method. Auditing the Company's United States accrued sales chargebacks and rebates owed pursuant to definitive contractual agreements or legal requirements with distributors, private (Managed Care and Group Purchasing Organizations) and public (Medicaid, Tricare, and Manufacturer's Discounts) benefit providers was challenging due to the extent of effort required to audit the significant number of sales chargeback and rebate programs, as the terms vary by distributor and program and by benefit provider. Additionally, due to the volume of sales chargebacks and rebates, third-party processing and the timing of invoicing received from distributors and benefit providers, the actual amounts incurred for all distributors and benefit providers are not known at the time the financial statements are issued. | Our audit procedures included, among others, the following: We evaluated and tested the design and the operating effectiveness of internal controls over the Company's process used in determining the measurement and completeness of accrued revenue rebates in the United States; We examined terms and conditions for a sample of contracts with the Company's customers and others in the distribution channel, tested a sample of credits issued and payments made throughout the year, and agreed rebate rates applied to the underlying contract terms; We tested the accuracy and completeness of the underlying data used in determining revenue rebates and evaluated the assumptions and inputs used by management. We performed analytical procedures in combination with confirmations of a sample of the inventory remained in the distribution channel at the year end; We performed substantive analytical procedures of the rebates accrued to total sales by program; We performed lookback analysis to evaluate the historical accuracy of the accrued revenue rebates estimates by comparing prior period accrued revenue rebates to the amount of actual payments made in subsequent periods; We checked the invoices received subsequently and compared with the accrued revenue rebates at the year end;
